sentences.text:
The present writ petition has been filed by the party-in-person seeking to challenge the award dated 6.4.2023 passed by the competent authority under Section 3G of the National Highways Act,
1956.

The prayer in the writ petition is to declare the award invalid, unlawful, unjust and direct the competent authority to re-assess, re-calculate by correct interpretation of Section 26(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013.

sentences.text: Various assertions have been made in the writ petition to challenge the market value applied by the competent authority for determination of the compensation.

On all the issues raised in the writ NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2378/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined petition,
appropriate remedy to the petitioner is to invoke the provisions of Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

3. At this stage, it is submitted by the petitioner (party-in-person) that he has already filed application before the competent authority for appointment of the Arbitrator and the Arbitrator is seized with the matter.
We do not find any reason to express any opinion on any observations of the Arbitrator as alleged in the writ petition as no final order has been passed.

Even otherwise, if the petitioner is aggrieved by the determination made by the Arbitrator, remedy before him is to approach the competent Courts under Sections 34 and 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996.
For the aforesaid, we do not find any reason to entertain the present writ petition.

(SUNITA AGARWAL, CJ ) (ANIRUDDHA P. MAYEE, J.) KAUSHIK D. CHAUHAN Vishnu Kumar Garg vs The Competent Authority Land ... on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190054925/
